items.headline: Jailed Jantar Mantar protesters move High Court
items.text: Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, held since 13 October for entering the closed Jantar Mantar protest site, asked the Delhi High Court on Tuesday for an urgent hearing, saying their custody breaches their right to liberty. The magistrate who extended it found their sureties unsatisfactory and said they could breach the peace.

photo.alt: A tall red and beige stone instrument with arched openings, on a lawn.
photo.caption: The Jantar Mantar observatory in New Delhi. The road beside it was the capital's main protest site until police denotified it this month.

items.headline: Shutdown in Manipur valley after villagers killed
items.text: Markets, schools and offices shut across five valley districts on Tuesday in a 48-hour strike after three Meitei villagers were shot dead on Monday; organisers demand arrests within 48 hours. Officials said extra forces were deployed, and police reported no incidents.

photo.alt: Women vendors selling vegetables, fish and grain on the floor of a covered market, seen from above.
photo.caption: Ima Keithel, the women's market in central Imphal. Markets across the valley were closed for the strike.

items.headline: Over 1,100 families evicted in Assam forest drive
items.text: Authorities evicted more than 1,100 families, mostly Bengali-speaking Muslims, from forest land over two days; residents say they lived there for decades and that more than 10 mosques were demolished. The state says it is reclaiming reserve forest after a court rejected their claims, and no immediate rehabilitation was reported.

items.headline: Drone strike near Kordofan market kills dozens
items.text: A drone hit a transport hub near the market in al-Dabab, an RSF-held town, on Sunday evening, killing 80 people according to residents and medics, or about 150 according to local groups. The RSF-aligned Tasis alliance blamed an army drone; the reports carry no army response.

items.place: Gaza City and Khan Younis, Gaza
items.headline: Couple and teenager among four killed in Gaza
items.text: Medics said an Israeli airstrike killed a couple in their Gaza City apartment on Tuesday, and gunfire killed a 17-year-old in Khan Younis and one person in Zeitoun. Israel's military said it struck a militant in Gaza City and did not immediately comment on the shootings.

photo.alt: People in dark clothing stand among plastic-sheet tents in heavy rain on muddy ground.
photo.caption: Flooded tents of displaced Palestinians after heavy rain in Deir el-Balah, Gaza.
photo.credit: Ashraf Amra / UNRWA, via Wikimedia Commons

items.place: Magwe, Sagaing, Mandalay, Rakhine and Chin, Myanmar
items.headline: Airstrikes kill at least 27 civilians in Myanmar
items.text: Military airstrikes from 16 to 18 October killed at least 27 civilians in five regions and states, The Irrawaddy reports, including 12 to 15 people at a WiFi shop in Yesagyo. The regime's defence minister called the operations steps toward peace.

items.headline: Eighth day of protest clashes in Tirana
items.text: Police fired tear gas and water cannon at student-led protesters on Tuesday, the eighth straight day of clashes, as some protesters threw rocks, flares and firebombs. The Prime Minister again refused to resign and said attempts to overthrow the government will not be allowed.

photo.alt: A large lawn in a city square with an equestrian statue, a minaret, a tower block and a red flag.
photo.caption: Skanderbeg Square in central Tirana.

items.headline: Iran arrests dozens more over winter protests
items.text: Qazvin's intelligence directorate said it arrested 39 people over the winter anti-government protests (VOA's headline says 38), accusing them of arson, looting and killing security personnel. Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch have called similar charges against protesters fabricated.

focus.title: Smoke since August
focus.dek: Fires in Kalimantan and Sumatra have burned more than 1.9 million hectares this year, a satellite monitor says, and sent smoke across Southeast Asia. Indonesia's government calls the haze largely natural; researchers and environmental groups say people lit the fires.
focus.alt: At night, flames and smoke rise from scrubland behind a lit campus building, with a fire engine on the road in front.
